Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary assessment: Reproductive-age female with several days of progressively worsening lower abdominal pain, midline below the umbilicus, constant in nature, plus light vaginal bleeding/discharge. On Implanon contraception. Last menses ~2 weeks ago. Nausea reported; constipation weeks prior but currently controlled. No fever or dyspnea noted. A face-to-face abdominal examination is planned to further localize pain and guide management. A pregnancy test today is recommended to evaluate pregnancy-related etiologies.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx; see ranked list below):
  - Ovarian cyst rupture / corpus luteum cyst — High
    • Rationale: lower abdominal pain, midline location, constant and worsening; concurrent light vaginal bleeding; reproductive-age female with recent menses history and implant use.
  - Pregnancy-related (ectopic pregnancy or threatened abortion / early intrauterine pregnancy) — Moderate
    • Rationale: vaginal bleeding with lower abdominal pain in a reproductive-age patient on contraception; pregnancy status remains a critical differential requiring evaluation.
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) — Moderate
    • Rationale: lower abdominal pain with vaginal discharge/bleeding in a sexually active young woman; may present afebrile.
- Conflicts: No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.

Management Plan
- Schedule in-person abdominal examination (clinic visit arranged via support line); clinician to perform abdominal exam and advise further based on findings.
- Pregnancy testing today: perform pregnancy test today; if positive, patient to be seen urgently; if negative, proceed with differential workup as guided by exam.
- Return precautions: if pain worsens or patient is unable to hold fluids, seek evaluation sooner.
